a1-n-beruf: A new friend asks what you do every day to earn money. You say that you are a nurse.
On the form there is a box that asks what you work as, for example teacher or driver.
A child says that when he grows up he wants to be a pilot. What is the word for this kind of work that you train for?
a1-pr-es: You look out of the window and say that water is falling from the sky. Which small word is the subject in 'it is raining'?
You point at the baby and say that it is sleeping. Which pronoun replaces a neuter noun like 'the baby'?
A friend asks about the time and you answer: it is half past two. Which small word starts the sentence?
a1-adv-daneben: You look at the pharmacy and say that the bakery is right at its side, on the same street. Which adverb means 'next to it'?
The waiter says that there is a table at the window and one at the side of it, free as well. Which adverb?
The man says that he works as a teacher and, in addition to that, he plays in a band. Which adverb means 'besides'?
a1-v-fruehstuecken: On Sunday morning you sit with your family at the table with rolls, jam and coffee, and eat the first meal of the day.
The hotel guests go to the dining room at eight o'clock to eat rolls and eggs.
A friend asks what you do at 7 o'clock with your coffee and toast. Which verb?
a1-n-bekannte: At the supermarket you meet a man whom you know a little, but he is not a close friend.
You say that the man in the street is someone that you met once at a party, so you only know him a little.
A woman says that she will go to the cinema with a man whom she knows slightly. Who is he?
a1-n-herbst: The leaves on the trees turn red and yellow and fall to the ground, and the days become shorter.
After summer and before winter there is a season with wind, rain and apples.
A friend asks which season comes between summer and winter. Which season?
a1-n-bahnhof: You carry your suitcase to the place where trains arrive and depart, with platforms and a ticket office.
The taxi driver asks where to take you, and you say: to the place where I can take the train to Berlin.
At the end of the journey the train stops and all the passengers get off at the big building with platforms. What is it?
a1-v-sein: The teacher asks you how old you are. You say that you are twenty-five. Which verb is needed in 'I am'?
A friend asks where you are. You say that you are at home. Which verb is used?
You say: the weather is nice today. Which very common verb is used for 'is'?
a1-n-laden: You walk into a small place in the street where you can buy shoes and clothes.
At the corner there is a place where the owner sells milk, bread and newspapers.
The sign on the door says that the place is open from nine to six. What kind of place is it?
a1-adj-blau: On a sunny day the sky is clear and has this colour, like the sea.
A child draws the sea and chooses the crayon with the colour of water.
The jeans are a dark version of this colour, like the colour of the ocean.
a1-n-geld: At the cash desk of the shop you give notes and coins to the cashier.
You work all week and at the end of the month the bank pays you your salary. What do you receive?
A friend says that he cannot go on holiday because he does not have enough of what you use to buy things.
a1-n-gespraech: You sit with your neighbour at the table and talk for an hour about the weather and your families.
The boss invites you to his office to talk with you about your work.
A friend says that after the exchange of words on the phone with his mother he feels better. What noun?
a1-v-einladen: You write to your friends and ask them to come to your birthday party on Saturday.
Your neighbour says that he would like you to come to his house for dinner tonight.
The workers put boxes into the van, one after another, until it is full. Which verb?
a1-adv-gleich: A friend calls and asks where you are. You say that you will be there in a minute, very soon. Which adverb?
The waiter says to the guests that the food will come in no time, without delay. Which adverb?
The teacher says that the two children are the same age. They are old in the same way. Which adverb means 'equally'?
a1-n-bett: After a long day you go to the room with the soft mattress and the pillow to sleep.
In the hotel there is a big piece of furniture with two pillows and a blanket in the room.
The child is tired and the mother puts him into the place where he sleeps at night.
a1-n-lokal: On Friday evening you meet your friends in a small place where you can have a beer and talk.
A friend recommends a place in town with good food and nice atmosphere, with a menu and waiters.
The man goes to a place after work, where he can order a beer or a meal, with tables and a counter.
a1-v-lernen: Every evening you sit at your desk and repeat words from your book to remember them for the test.
The child gets to know the letters of the alphabet at school, step by step.
Your friend asks what you do in the language school. You say that you gain knowledge about German.
a1-n-pause: After two hours of lessons the teacher says that you can have a rest for fifteen minutes.
At work you leave the desk at noon, to eat your sandwich and drink coffee.
In the middle of the film there is a short stop, so that the audience can buy a drink.
a1-adj-fertig: You cooked for an hour and now you say that the food is complete and on the table.
The teacher asks if you have completed the exercise. You say yes, I have no more to do.
A friend asks if you are prepared to leave. You say yes, I have my coat and my keys. Which adjective?
a1-n-wiederhoeren: At the end of a phone call to a company, the clerk says a polite phrase meaning 'goodbye until we speak again'.
At the end of a radio programme the host says goodbye to the people who are listening, hoping they will tune in again.
You finish a phone call with your teacher and want to say a polite goodbye that only works on the phone, not face to face.
a1-pr-ihnen-2: A stranger on the street asks you for the way. You politely ask: can I help you? Which word means 'you' in the polite form, as an indirect object?
The clerk says to a customer: I thank you for your patience. Which polite pronoun is used?
Your boss says to a visitor: this gift is for you. In the polite form, which word is used?
a1-n-postleitzahl: On the envelope you write the number of five digits, such as 10115, before the name of the town.
The online shop asks for your street, house number and the number for your area, so that the parcel can arrive.
On the form: street, city and the number that helps the post office to sort the mail. What is it called?
a1-v-trinken: After the long walk you take the bottle and swallow water in big mouthfuls.
At breakfast the children have milk or juice in a glass. What do they do with it?
The waiter asks what you want with your meal. You say you would like a glass of wine and take a sip. Which verb describes this?
a1-n-meter: The room is 4 of these long. What unit of length is it?
A tailor measures the cloth. One of these is a hundred centimetres.
The athlete runs a hundred of these in the race. Which unit?
a1-n-klasse: At school you sit with twenty other pupils of the same age in a room, with one teacher.
The teacher says that the pupils in her group are very noisy today.
On the train you buy a ticket for the second level, which is cheaper than the first level.
a1-adv-jetzt: You are asked when you want to start. You say: at this moment, not later. Which adverb?
The teacher says: no, not tomorrow, but at this moment we start the test. Which adverb?
A friend asks if you are still working. You say: at present I am at home. Which adverb means 'currently'?
a1-adj-falsch: The teacher marks your answer in the test with a cross. It is not correct.
You take the bus in the wrong direction and arrive at a place you did not want to go to.
The statement says that the sun goes round the Earth. Is it true? No, it is ...
a1-n-pfund: At the market you ask for a pound of cheese, an old unit of about half a kilo.
In an English recipe the weight is given in lbs. Which unit is this?
The baker says that the loaf weighs one of these, between 400 and 500 grams. Which unit?
a1-v-riechen: You walk past the bakery and notice the delicious scent of fresh bread with your nose.
The milk is old. You hold it near your face and notice a bad odour.
The flowers in the garden give off a sweet scent. What do you do with your nose?
a1-n-preis: You look at the label on the jacket and see that it costs 80 euros. What is the amount called?
At the sports day the winner receives a gold cup. What is the cup called?
A friend asks how much the ticket is. You tell him the amount you paid. Which noun?
a1-n-test: The teacher says that tomorrow there will be a short written examination in vocabulary.
Before you begin the course, the school asks you to do a short exercise to find out your level.
The doctor sends your blood to the lab to check for illness. What do you call this check?
a1-v-wissen: The teacher asks the capital of France and you are sure that you have the information: Paris.
A friend asks if you have heard that the shop is closed. You say: yes, I am aware of that.
A tourist asks you for the way and you say that you do not have the information. Which verb means 'to be aware of a fact'?
a1-n-essen: At noon the whole family sits at the table and the mother serves soup and meat.
At the canteen the workers go at 12 o'clock to have lunch. What do they eat?
A friend invites you: come to our house on Saturday, we will have an evening meal. Which noun?
a1-n-reis: The cook boils small white grains in water and serves them with curry.
In Asia the farmers grow this plant in wet fields, and it is eaten with fish and vegetables every day.
At the Indian restaurant you order chicken with a side dish of white grains. What is the side dish?
a1-adj-klein: A mouse is not big, and an elephant is not small. Which adjective describes the mouse?
The flat has only one room and a tiny kitchen. It is not large at all.
A child is not tall for his age. The doctor says that he is quite short.
a1-n-text: The teacher gives you a page with a story and asks you to read it and answer the questions.
You write a message on your phone with words and sentences for your friend.
In the newspaper there is a picture, and below it there are several lines of words that explain it.
a1-v-wehtun: You fall off your bike and your knee gives you pain. You say that it hurts.
The dentist touches the tooth and you say that you feel pain. Which verb?
The child says to his mother that his head aches. What does his head do?
a1-adv-warum: A child sees that his mother is sad and asks for the reason. Which question word?
You come late to the party and your friend asks you for the cause. Which question word?
The teacher says that nobody knows the reason for the strange noise, and asks: for what reason did it happen? Which question word?
a1-n-flasche: At the supermarket you buy a drink in a container with a narrow neck, made of glass or plastic.
The baby is hungry and the mother gives him milk in a container with a rubber nipple.
At the restaurant the waiter brings a container of wine and opens it with a corkscrew.
a1-n-alter: The doctor asks how many years old you are. You say: twenty-five. What is this number called?
On the form there is a box where you write the number of years since birth.
The film has the label: only for people over 16 years of age. What is this quantity called?
a1-pr-wenig: There are only a small number of people at the party. Which word means 'not many'?
You have only a small amount of time before the train leaves. Which word means 'not much'?
A friend asks if you have money, and you say that you have just a little. Which word expresses a small quantity?
a1-n-welt: A traveller says that he wants to see all the countries and oceans of the Earth.
The news reports that people from every country watch the final of the football cup, from Asia to America.
A child looks at the globe and asks what it is. It is a model of the planet where we live.
a1-v-ankreuzen: In the test you put a cross in the box next to the correct answer.
At the election the voter puts a cross next to the name of the party.
The form says: please put a mark in the right box. Which verb means to mark a box with a cross?
a1-n-monat: There are twelve of these in a year, and each has about thirty days.
You pay your rent on the first day of each one of these.
The baby is only three of these old. Which unit of time?
a1-adj-verheiratet: The man wears a ring on his finger. He has a wife and says that he is not single.
On the form: single, divorced or ... You tick the box because you went to a wedding last year with your partner.
A woman says that she has been with her husband since her wedding twenty years ago. Which adjective describes her?
a1-n-auslaender: A man from Turkey lives in Germany and does not have a German passport. What is he called?
At the immigration office, the officer says that people who come from other countries must register.
In a country, a person who comes from another country and lives there for some time is called what?
a1-n-april: It is the month between March and May, when the weather changes a lot, sun and rain.
The children look for Easter eggs in this month, the fourth of the year.
On the first day of this month people play jokes on each other. Which month?
a1-v-kennenlernen: At the party you meet a person for the first time and talk to her for an hour.
On the first day at the new school, the pupils get acquainted with each other.
Your friend says that he met his wife on a train. What did he do with her at first?
a1-n-glueck: You win the lottery and everyone says that you are fortunate. What is that called?
You smile and feel joy, because your family is healthy and your life is good.
The friend says: I wish you success in the exam. He wants you to have what?
a1-adv-woher: You meet a new person at the party and ask about his home country. Which question word?
A friend gives you a nice cake and you ask: where is it from? Which question word?
The teacher asks the student: from which country do you come? Which question word?
a1-n-vater: On Father's Day the children give a present to the man who raised them.
A child calls out for the man who gets him from school every day, his male parent.
You introduce the man next to you as the husband of your mother. He is a male parent. Who?
a1-v-abgeben: At the end of the exam you give your paper to the teacher, so that she can check it.
At the reception you leave your coat with the clerk, who takes it for the evening.
You hand in the form at the office before Friday. Which verb means to hand in?
a1-n-sofa: In the evening you sit on a soft piece of furniture in the living room with cushions and watch TV.
A guest stays overnight and sleeps on the soft piece of furniture in the living room.
The cat sleeps on the soft seat for several people, in front of the television.
a1-adj-willkommen: The host opens the door and says that you are received with joy and invites you in.
A sign at the airport says that the visitors are greeted warmly. Which adjective?
The family is happy when the guests arrive. They say: you are very ... here.
a1-n-praxis: You have a pain in your back, so you make an appointment at the place where your doctor treats patients.
The sign on the door says that the surgery is open from 8 to 12.
The company wants an employee with experience in actually doing the work, not only from books. What do you call this kind of experience?
a1-n-herr: At the hotel the clerk says to a man: how can I help you? She uses a polite title for him.
On the envelope you write a polite title before the family name of a man.
At the beginning of a formal letter you write: Dear ... Müller. Which word is used for a man?
a1-v-zahlen: The waiter brings the bill and you take your wallet to give the amount in cash.
You buy a coffee and give the cashier two euros.
At the end of the month you hand over the rent to your landlord. What do you do with the money?
a1-n-studium: After school he spent five years at university, learning medicine, and then he became a doctor.
Your sister will begin her time at the university in October.
At the application form the question is about the time you spent at university. What noun?
a1-pr-ihm: You give a book to your brother. You say: I give a book to ... Which word is used for 'him' as an indirect object?
You ask about your friend and say: I phone ... every day. Which pronoun means 'him' as the indirect object?
The teacher says that you should help the new pupil, and say: help ... with the homework. Which word?
a1-n-hand: You meet a business partner and put out the part of your body at the end of your arm to say hello.
The child holds his mother's part of the body with five fingers when they cross the street.
The doctor looks at the part of your body with five fingers, because you cut it with a knife.
a1-adv-so: You show your child how to tie shoes: do it in this way. Which small word means 'in this way'?
A friend asks if the film was good and you say that it was extremely good. Which word means 'such' or 'that much'?
The teacher says: write the letter like this, and shows an example. Which small word?
a1-adj-schoen: You look at the lake, the mountains and the flowers and say that it is very pleasing to the eye.
The weather is sunny and warm. You say that it is pleasant today.
A friend shows you her new dress and you say that it looks lovely. Which adjective?
a1-n-reparatur: The car does not work, so the mechanic says that he will fix it and the work will cost 200 euros.
The sign in the window says: we do the work of mending your phone, in one hour.
The washing machine has stopped, so you call a technician to do the job of making it work again. What noun?
a1-v-abholen: After school the mother stands at the gate and takes her child home.
The parcel is at the post office and you walk there to take it with you.
A friend says that he will come to your house at 7 o'clock with his car and take you to the party.
a1-n-achtung: A sign on the road says: be careful, the surface is wet. What is the single word at the top?
At the station a voice says that you must stand back from the edge of the platform, with a warning word first.
You show your respect for an old person, giving him the regard that he deserves. Which noun?
a1-n-kuehlschrank: You put milk, cheese and butter into a big cold box in the kitchen so that they stay fresh.
The ice cream melts, because you left it on the table instead of putting it in the cold place in the kitchen.
At the shop you buy an electric machine, which keeps food cold, together with a freezer.
a1-v-telefonieren: Every evening you sit on the sofa and speak to your mother over the line for an hour.
The boss says that he is in a conversation on the phone and cannot be disturbed right now.
You call your friend in another country with your mobile. What is the action?
a1-n-fuss: The shoes are too small and the part of your body at the end of your leg hurts.
The dancer stands on the tips of the parts of her body that are in her shoes.
The doctor asks you to step on the scale with the parts of your body at the bottom of the legs. What is it?
a1-n-wind: In autumn the air moves strongly, and the leaves fly around, and your hat flies away.
On the beach the sailors are happy, because the air moves and fills the sails.
The weather report says that tomorrow there will be strong moving air from the west. What noun?
a1-adj-leicht: The test is not difficult at all. Everybody finishes it in ten minutes.
The bag weighs only two kilos. It is not heavy and you can carry it with one hand.
The jacket is thin and weighs almost nothing. Which adjective describes its weight?
a1-n-dank: After the help of your neighbour you say: many thanks. What noun expresses what you feel?
At the end of the speech the president expresses his gratitude to all the people who helped.
A card says: with deep gratitude for your help. What noun is it?
a1-v-werden: The boy was small last year and next year he will be tall. What does he do with respect to size?
You say that tomorrow you will go to the cinema. Which verb expresses the future?
It is cold in the morning, but in the afternoon it will get warm. Which verb describes the change?
a1-n-ankunft: On the screen at the airport you see the time when the plane from Rome lands. What is the information?
Your friend phones to say that she will be there at 5 o'clock, when the train reaches the station.
At the train station a sign says 'Arrivals and Departures'. What is the opposite of departure?
a1-adv-sofort: The boss says that you must come to his office this very second, without waiting. Which adverb?
The doctor says that you should take the medicine without delay, at once.
You call the taxi and the driver says that he will be there straight away. Which adverb?
a1-n-uhr: You look at the wall in the kitchen to see that it is already 8 o'clock.
Your grandfather gives you a small device that you wear on your wrist to show the time.
The train leaves at 9 ... Which word means 'o'clock', or also the instrument that shows the time?
a1-n-kugelschreiber: At the bank, you write your name on the form with a writing tool with a small ball at the tip and blue ink.
You buy a small plastic writing instrument with a clicking button in the stationery shop.
The teacher says that tests must not be written with a pencil but with a blue writing instrument. What is it?
a1-v-antworten: The teacher asks a question and you give your reply in a loud voice.
You receive an email from your boss, and write back the same day.
A friend asks if you are coming to the party. You say: yes. What did you do?
a1-n-fax: Before email, the office used a machine to send paper copies over the phone line.
The lawyer asks you to send the contract by a machine that scans the paper and sends it over a telephone line.
The old office has a printer, a telephone and a machine for sending documents over the phone line.
a1-pr-mein: You show a photo and say that this is the car that belongs to you. Which word means 'belonging to me'?
You introduce a person: this is the sister who belongs to me. Which possessive word?
At the airport the officer asks whose bag it is. You say: it belongs to me. Which word means 'my' or 'mine'?
a1-adj-leise: At night the baby is sleeping, so you speak with a soft voice and walk without noise.
In the library the librarian asks everybody not to talk loudly. Which adjective?
The new electric car makes almost no sound. Which adjective describes it?
a1-n-eingang: At the entrance of the cinema there is a queue of people who wait to get in.
You look for the door where you can come into the building, and the sign says: use the door at the side.
The letter of the bank arrives on Monday. The date of its arrival is written down as receipt.
a1-v-sich-kuemmern: Your neighbour is on holiday, so you give water to her plants and feed her cat. You take responsibility.
The mother looks after her sick child and gives him medicine.
The teacher says that you must arrange the project yourself. Which verb means to take care of something?
a1-n-zimmer: In the hotel you get the key for a place with a bed, a window and a bathroom, number 305.
The flat has a kitchen, a bathroom and three of these: a living room and two bedrooms.
A student rents a place with a bed and a desk in a shared flat. What do you call each space?
a1-n-ordnung: The teacher says that your desk is a mess, and that you must put everything in the right place. What is it?
Your mother looks into your room and is happy: everything is clean and in its place.
In the rules for the library, the books must be in the sequence of the alphabet. What is it called?
a1-adv-schnell: The runner crosses the finish line at high speed. Which adverb describes how he runs?
The teacher says: please answer in a short time, do not wait. Which adverb?
A friend says: come soon, we do not have much time. Which adverb describes the way you should come?
a1-n-glueckwunsch: You hear that your friend has passed the exam and you say 'well done' with a smile.
On your birthday you receive many cards and messages with kind words about your day.
After the wedding, the guests tell the bride and the groom that they are happy for them. What noun?
a1-v-scheinen: After the rain the sun comes out and gives light and warmth to the garden.
The man looks very tired. You say that he gives the impression of not having slept.
The text says that the shop is closed, although the light is on. Which verb means 'to give the impression'?
a1-n-baby: The young mother carries a very small child who is only three months old and sleeps all day.
At the hospital the nurse brings the newborn to the mother.
A couple buys a small bed, tiny clothes and a pram, because their child will soon be born.
a1-adj-alt: The man with white hair and a stick is eighty years of age. He is not young.
The church in the town centre was built in the year 1200. It is not new.
You do not buy the car because it has been used for twenty years and looks worn. Which adjective?
a1-n-bauch: After a big meal you feel full, and the front part of your body below the chest is round and hurts.
The doctor says that you have a pain in the part of the body where the stomach is.
The child says that he has pain in his tummy. Which part of the body?
a1-n-gleis: At the station the voice says that the train to Hamburg will leave from number 7, where you wait on the platform.
The train drives on steel lines in the ground. What are these lines called?
At the station the sign says: do not cross the lines. What are they?
a1-v-kommen: A friend phones you and asks if you will visit him this evening. You say: yes, I will be there at 8 o'clock.
The train arrives at the station at 10:15. What does it do?
The teacher says to a pupil outside: please enter the room. Which verb describes coming towards the speaker?
a1-n-angebot: In the supermarket there is a sign with a special price for tomatoes this week.
The shop clerk says that the shop has a large selection of jackets in different sizes.
A company writes to you and says that it will do the work for 500 euros. What do you call this written price proposal?
a1-n-ausland: After school she goes to live in France, Spain and Italy, in other countries than hers.
The company sends its employees to work in a country that is not their home country. Where do they go?
A friend says: I will go on holiday not in my own country but somewhere else, on the other side of the border.
a1-v-ausfuellen: At the bank the clerk gives you a paper with empty boxes, and you write your name and address into them.
At the doctor's reception you must write information in the boxes of the paper.
The teacher says that you should put the missing words into the gaps of the sentence.
a1-n-ergebnis: After the exam the teacher tells you your mark. What is it?
The football match is over, and the newspaper says 2:1. What do you call this?
The doctor tells you the outcome of the blood test on the phone. What noun?
a1-adj-gerade: The road runs for ten kilometres without any curve. It is not curved at all.
You draw a line with a ruler on the paper. It is not bent. Which adjective?
The number 4 is not odd, but ... Which adjective describes numbers like 2, 4 and 6?
a1-adv-heute: You ask your friend if he has plans for this day, not tomorrow. Which adverb?
The teacher says that the test will be written on this day, not on another day.
Nowadays most people have a mobile phone. In contrast with the past, what adverb means 'at the present time'?
a1-n-feiertag: On December 25th, all shops are closed and most people do not work. What kind of day is it?
On the first of January nobody goes to the office, because it is a day off for everybody in the country.
On the calendar some days are marked in red, such as Christmas and Easter. What are these days?
a1-pr-du: You meet a friend and ask how he is. Which word means 'you' for a close friend, a child or a family member?
A boy says to his sister: are you coming with me to the shop? Which pronoun is used for 'you' in the informal form?
Two students who are friends talk to each other: what pronoun means 'you' for one person informally?
